questions.text: What is Dynamic Confidence and what problem does it address?

answer.text: Dynamic Confidence is a lightweight, parameter-insensitive, on-the-fly method that optimizes latency dynamically at runtime for Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) [2]. It addresses the problem of efficiently reducing latency and power consumption in SNNs while maintaining performance [3].

questions.text: What is confidence saturation and how do the authors prevent it?

answer.text: Confidence saturation refers to the phenomenon where the confidence estimate ˆPt quickly reaches 100% and stops improving with time t, making it less effective as an estimator of ˆYt = Y [1]. To prevent this, the authors introduce a scalar regulation parameter α to restrict the scale of the output logits in SNNs, calculating confidence as ˆPt = max( ezi t/α PK j=1 ezj t/α ) for i = 1, 2, . . . , K [3].

questions.text: How is the confidence threshold chosen?

answer.text: The confidence threshold thc is chosen using a low-cost Pareto Front method to compute the precise confidence threshold [2]. This method discretizes the search space of thc with a resolution of 0.1, resulting in 11 settings of thc [2]. The selection of thc reflects the fundamental latency-accuracy trade-off in SNNs [1]. The Pareto Front method is used to find thc values that achieve the highest accuracy for each latency [2].

questions.text: Which datasets and network architectures were used in the experiments?

answer.text: The experiments were conducted on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet datasets. For CIFAR-10, the network architectures used were VGG-16 and ResNet-18. For ImageNet, the architectures used were VGG-16 and ResNet-50 [1].

questions.text: How much latency does Dynamic Confidence save on ImageNet with ResNet-50?

answer.text: Dynamic Confidence saves 26% to 36% latency on ImageNet without sacrificing accuracy [1]. Not found in the paper.

questions.text: What accuracy could an ideal decision-making agent reach on ImageNet and in how many time steps?

answer.text: An ideal decision-making agent could reach an accuracy of 82.47% on ImageNet within just 4.71 time steps [2].

questions.text: On which GPU were the latency measurements made?

answer.text: The latency measurements were made on an NVIDIA-V100 GPU [1].

questions.text: What did the authors measure on Intel Loihi neuromorphic chips?

answer.text: The authors did not measure anything on Intel Loiromorphic chips. Not found in the paper.
